title: Understand the Benefits of and Strategies for Migration to the AWS Cloud

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Moving to AWS is not simply copying everything from a data center. Organizations need a cloud adoption strategy, migration resources, desired outcomes, and an approach suited to each workload.
bullets: Cloud adoption strategies
Resources that support the cloud migration journey
AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)
AWS CAF business outcomes
Appropriate migration strategies, including database replication and AWS Snowball
sections.callout: How can an organization plan and support its move to AWS, and what migration approach fits the situation?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
bullets: PLAN → Why are we adopting cloud?
PREPARE → Which organizational capabilities must be ready?
MOVE → How should the workload or data migrate?
IMPROVE → Which business outcomes are we pursuing?

sections.title: Cloud Adoption Strategies
paragraphs: A cloud adoption strategy directs how an organization will begin using cloud technologies. It aligns the migration with business objectives, organizational readiness, technical requirements, operational capabilities, risks, and desired outcomes.
bullets: Improve operational efficiency
Reduce business risk
Support business growth
Modernize technology
Increase organizational agility
Improve sustainability-related outcomes
sections.callout: Planning people, processes, technology, readiness, and goals → Cloud adoption strategy

sections.title: Resources for the Cloud Migration Journey
paragraphs: AWS guidance and assessment resources can help inventory workloads, evaluate readiness and dependencies, plan migration phases, and connect technical work to expected business outcomes.
sections.callout: Assess before moving: readiness, dependencies, risks, and outcomes.

sections.title: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)
paragraphs: AWS CAF helps organizations identify capabilities needed for successful cloud transformation. Cloud adoption affects business, people, governance, technology, security, and operations—not just servers.
sections.callout: AWS CAF = prepare the organization for cloud transformation.

entries.title: Reduced Business Risk
paragraphs: Improve how the organization identifies and manages operational, security, governance, and business risks.
entries.memoryHook: Reduce exposure and the impact of business problems.

entries.title: Improved ESG Performance
paragraphs: Support environmental, social, and governance objectives through the cloud transformation program.

entries.title: Increased Revenue
paragraphs: Use cloud capabilities to reach opportunities faster, support new offerings, and enable business growth.

entries.title: Increased Operational Efficiency
paragraphs: Streamline processes, reduce unnecessary effort, and use organizational resources more effectively.

sections.title: Selecting a Migration Strategy
paragraphs: Choose a migration method based on the workload, dependencies, data volume, operational constraints, network capacity, downtime tolerance, and business goals. One method does not fit every workload.
sections.callout: What is the appropriate way to move this workload or dataset?

sections.title: Database Replication
paragraphs: Database replication copies and synchronizes database changes between source and target systems. It is useful when an active database continues receiving inserts, updates, and deletes during migration.
bullets: Existing database
Source and target must remain synchronized
Changing data must continue to replicate
Reduce disruption before final cutover
sections.callout: Keep copying and synchronizing active database data → Database replication

sections.title: AWS Snowball
paragraphs: AWS Snowball uses a physical data-transfer device to move large datasets into or out of AWS when transferring the data over the available network would take too long or be impractical.
bullets: Very large data volume
Limited or slow network connection
Online transfer would take too long
Physical device is shipped for data transfer
sections.callout: Large offline data transfer when the network is impractical → AWS Snowball

sections.title: AWS CAF vs. Well-Architected Framework

table.caption: Choose the framework based on the scope of the question
rows: Prepare an organization for cloud adoption and transformation
Evaluate whether a cloud workload is architected and operated well

sections.callout: ADOPT/TRANSFORM WELL → AWS CAF. BUILD/OPERATE WELL → Well-Architected.

entries.title: AWS CAF vs. Well-Architected
paragraphs: Organizational cloud transformation → AWS CAF. Workload architecture and operations → Well-Architected Framework.

entries.title: Operational Efficiency vs. Operational Excellence
paragraphs: AWS CAF transformation outcome → Increased operational efficiency. Well-Architected pillar → Operational Excellence.

entries.title: ESG vs. Sustainability
paragraphs: Organization-wide environmental, social, and governance outcome → Improved ESG performance. Workload environmental impact pillar → Sustainability.

entries.title: Revenue vs. Cost Optimization
paragraphs: Grow business opportunities and income → Increased revenue. Avoid unnecessary workload spending → Cost Optimization.

entries.title: Database Replication vs. AWS Snowball
paragraphs: Continuously synchronize an active database → Database replication. Move a very large dataset with a physical device because the network is impractical → AWS Snowball.
